questions.q: The point in the interval $[0,2 \pi]$, where $f(x)=e^x \sin x$ has maximum slope, is
questions.solution:
We have, $f(x)=e^x \sin x\Rightarrow  f^{\prime}(x)=e^x \cos x+\sin x \cdot e^x$
and $f^{\prime \prime}(x)=-\sin x \cdot e^x+\cos x \cdot e^x+\cos x \cdot e^x+\sin x \cdot e^x$
Now, for maximum or minimum slope put $\left(f^{\prime}(x)\right)^{\prime}=0 \Rightarrow f^{\prime \prime}(x)=0\Rightarrow  2 \cos x \cdot e^x=0\Rightarrow \cos x=0 \Rightarrow x=\frac{\pi}{2}$
Also, $f^{\prime \prime \prime}(x)=-2 \sin x \cdot e^x+2 \cos x \cdot e^x=$ negative
$\therefore$ Slope is maximum at $x=\pi / 2$.

The equations of the asymptotes of the hyperbola

questions.solution:
Here, $\alpha=2 \theta, \beta=\theta$
Time of flight of $A$ is, $\begin{aligned} T_1 & =\frac{2 u \sin (\alpha-\beta)}{g \cos \beta} \\ & =\frac{2 u \sin (2 \theta-\theta)}{g \cos \theta} \\ & =\frac{2 u}{g} \tan \theta \end{aligned}$ Time of flight of $B$ is, $T_2=\frac{2 u \sin \theta}{g \cos \theta}=\frac{2 u}{g} \tan \theta$ So, $T_1=T_2$. The acceleration of both the particles is $g$ downwards. Therefore, relative acceleration between the two is zero or relative motion between the two is uniform. questions.q: Two bodies $A$ and $B$ having temperatlires $327^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and $427^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ are radiating heat to the surrounding. The surrounding temperature is $27^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The ratio of rates of heat radiation of $A$ to that of $B$ is

If temperature of surrounding is considered, then net loss of energy of a body by radiation
$Q=\operatorname{Ae\sigma }\left(T^4-T_0^4\right) \Rightarrow Q \propto\left(T^4-T_0^4\right)\therefore  \frac{Q_1}{Q_2}=\frac{T_1^4-T_0^4}{T_2^4-T_0^4}=\frac{(273+327)^4-(273+27)^4}{(273+427)^4-(273+27)^4}=\frac{(600)^4-(300)^4}{(700)^4-(300)^4}=0.52$

questions.solution:
Let $n_1$ and $n_2$ be the frequencies of the two notes of wavelengths $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$.
Here, $\lambda_1=1 \mathrm{~m}, \lambda_2=1.01 \mathrm{~m}$
If $v$ is velocity of sound, then
$n_1=\frac{v}{1} \text { and } n_2=\frac{v}{1.01}$
If the number of beats produced per second is $b$, then
$\begin{aligned}
& b=n_1-n_2 \\
& 4=\frac{v}{1}-\frac{v}{1.01} \\
&\therefore v=\frac{4.04}{0.01}=404 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A string fixed at both ends oscillates in 5 segments, length 10 m and velocity of wave is $20 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. What is the frequency?
questions.solution:
Frequency of vibration is given by
$n=\frac{p}{2 l} \sqrt{\frac{T}{m}} \left(\text { where } v=\sqrt{\frac{T}{m}}\right)\therefore n=\frac{p v}{2 l}=\frac{5 \times 20}{2 \times 10}=5 \mathrm{~Hz}$
